Title: Copy/Paste Tack
Content: Objective Copy and paste tack. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack Operation Copy/Paste Tack Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Copy The selected tack is copied. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. Select Paste or Mirror Paste. Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. Any tack outside of the Pattern does not appear in the 3D window. Click the desired location to paste the tack. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the tack to be duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. Selected tack is duplicated to the exact same location on its Symmetric Pattern. Note: Selected tacks need to be within the same Pattern in order to be duplicated to their Symmetric Patterns.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for copying, pasting, and duplicating tacks in a sewing pattern using the 3D toolbar for efficient garment design.

Title: Edit/Delete Tack
Content: Objective Edit the position and the spacing of tacks/Avatar or delete unnecessary tacks. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack Operation Edit Tack Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment is now being changed to semi-transparent. Click drag on the end point to adjust the position and spacing. Delete Tack Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack Click on a tack to delete. The selected tack is now being highlighted in yellow color. Press 'Delete' on the keyboard, or right-click and select Delete among the pop-up menu option. The selected tack is now being deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides users with tools and instructions to edit the position, spacing, and visibility of sewing tacks in a 3D garment interface, including options to delete unnecessary tacks.

Title: Line Tack on Garment
Content: Objective Create lines on Garment and tack to each other by lines / shapes. (Ver. MD7) Location 3D window tool bar Line tack tool Operation Select the tool according to the Location above. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the Line Tack Tool in the 3D window to create, manipulate, and simulate connections between garment shapes efficiently.

Title: Line Tack on Avatar
Content: Objective Create lines on Garment and avatar and tack to each other by lines. (Ver. MD7) Location 3D window tool bar Line tack on Avatar tool Operation Select the tool according to the Location above. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Once a line is created on the garment, 3D garment will be transparent, can create line on the avatar directly. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the 3D window tool to create and manipulate lines and shapes on garments and avatars, ensuring accurate tacking and simulation.

Title: Edit Line Tack
Content: Objective Edit created line tack's points / thread length of lines on "Property Editor". (Ver. MD7) Location 3D window tool bar Edit Line tack tool Operation Select the tool according to the Location above. Select and move points created with Line Tack. Can delete points create with Line Tack. After Selecting a Point, input Delete Key on the Keyboard. After Selecting a Point, right click and select Delete menu. Created Line Tack Lines can be reversed. Select created line, Right click and select Reverse Line Tack Menu. Setting distance between created lines. When selecting a line created with Line Tack, Thread Length menu will appear to Property Editor. Can set distance between lines by inputting value to Thread Length menu.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to using the Line Tack tool in the Property Editor (Ver. MD7) for editing points, adjusting thread lengths, and managing line configurations in the 3D window.

Title: [Beta] AI Graphic Generator (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Easily type in keywords to generate different graphic images to choose from to create new graphics. Location Graphic Property Material Basic Parameters AI Graphic Generator button Operation Create a pattern piece to place a graphic on. Add a graphic to the pattern using the add Graphic (2D Pattern) Tool Select the Graphic in the 2D window. Under Graphic Properties AI Graphic Generator button to the right of the Basic Parameters AI Graphic Generator window appears. Set Content Type, Transparent Background, enter prompts and click the Generate button. Check the generated graphic in the preview window. The generated graphic is stored in History. Click generate again to generate more Graphic images. Click Apply button, the selected image is applied as the Graphic. Generate AI Graphic Options Content Type Select the type of content for the graphic to be generated. None Create an image without specifying characteristics of the graphic image. Art Set the characteristics of the graphic image: Embroidery, Patch, Pop Art Transparent Background Apply a transparent background to the image. Note: This option is not available for the Pop Art type. Text Prompt Enter the prompt. Writing Tips: List words. Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. Emphasize certain words more than others. If parentheses are used in the word you want to emphasize, it takes up more weight. Parentheses on certain words take more weight. Weight increase rate: (word) 1.1 times, ((word)) 1.21 times. Maintain Prompt Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Graphic image is newly created each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while maintaining the characteristics of the previously generated result as much as possible. Note: It may differ from the existing results depending on the addition or change of the prompts. Random The sample prompt is randomly applied. This option automatically changes to a type specific to the prompt. History Previously generated images with prompts are recorded as "histories". The history remains accessible until Marvelous Designer is closed. If you select a previously created image in History and click Apply, the image is applied as Texture. Note: It may take a while to create when there are many users generating AI graphic images at the same time. The resulting generated images are only a preview until Apply is selected.
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly generate and customize unique graphic images by entering keywords and utilizing advanced AI tools to enhance your designs."

Title: Flip Graphic Image Horizontally/Vertically
Content: Objective Flip graphic images horizontally or vertically (only available in the 2D window). Location 2D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically The selected graphic image is now being flipped accordingly.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for flipping graphic images horizontally or vertically using the 2D toolbar and right-click graphics menu.

Title: Edit Graphic Size (Property Editor)
Content: Objective Use the Property Editor to resize graphics. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) /Transform Graphic Operation Follow the indicated guideline in Location Select the graphic to be edited. The selected graphic's properties appear in the Property Editor. Find the Graphic Transformation category. Properties Description Information Name/Item No. Enter a name or an item number of the graphic. Classification Assign the graphic type among Embroidery, Logo, Print, Wash (Jeanologia). Material Configure the graphic's material, texture, color, and transparency. Graphic Configuration Face Place the graphic on the front, back, or both sides. Over Seamline (ver MD10) Place the graphic on the seam of patterns. Note: - Graphic does not appear when the difference of the seam is over the allowable extent. - Graphic may not be matching when it is placed over the curves. It this case, deactivate this option and adjust the graphic manually. Tile Tile the graphic along the X or Y axis of a Pattern while maintaining its original size. Note: The same option is available in the right-click pop-up menu. Graphic Transformation Adjust the rotation angle, width, height, and Z-Offset(ver MD10) of the graphic.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the Property Editor to efficiently resize and configure graphics within the 2D pattern editing interface.

Title: Graphic Configuration
Content: Objective Configure graphics to repeat along the x-axis, y-axis, or all over the pattern. Use this function when graphics are used repeatedly on a Garment. Location Via the Property Editor Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) Via the Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic Right-Click (on Graphic) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-Click (on Graphic) Operation Via the Property Editor Follow the path: Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) The properties of the selected graphic will appear in the Property Editor. Find the Tile menu in the Property Editor and adjust the settings below as needed: Option Description Revert to Original Reset the graphic to its original configuration before this function was used. X-Axis Repeat the graphic along the x-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Y-Axis Repeat the graphic along the y-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Pattern Repeat the graphic across the entire pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. Via the Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Follow the path: Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic Right-Click (on Graphic) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-Click (on Graphic) Right-click pop-up menu appears. Navigate to Tile and select from the available options (same as Property Editor). The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. Note: When a graphic is repeated using this function, its Graphic Transformation Original Width and Original Height values will change.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to configure and repeat graphics along the x-axis, y-axis, or across an entire pattern in garment design using the Property Editor and toolbar options.

Title: Apply Normal Map To Graphic Image
Content: Objective Apply Normal Maps to graphics for more realistic visualization. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic Select a graphic image to apply Normal Map. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Material Texture Normal Map The intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be applied automatically as entered. The higher the value, the bumpier expression, the less the value, the less bumpier expression.
ContentDescription: "Enhance your graphics with realistic depth and texture by applying Normal Maps through our intuitive 2D Pattern Edit interface."

Title: Transform Graphic
Content: Objective Select and move graphic. Location Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic 2D/ 3D Toolbar graphic.png Transform Graphic Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline above: Click a graphic. The graphic is selected. When graphics are overlapped, a pop-up window appears allowing users to select the desired graphic (ver MD10). Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select other graphics. Multiple graphics are selected. Or, click and drag in the 2D window. All graphics in the marquee box are selected. Scale Follow the indicated guideline above: Click and drag or use the arrow keys to move graphics. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while dragging the graphics (ver5.0.0.) The graphics move vertically, horizontally, or diagonally at 45. Or, right click or hit the F1(Mac: Ctrl) key to input Distance Moved. Note: Sizing graphic up/down/left/right using Gizmo is only available in 2D Window When graphic over the seamline, it is transformed keeping the original setting. (ver MD10)
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for selecting and moving graphics in both 2D and 3D environments, including tips for handling overlapping graphics and utilizing keyboard shortcuts for efficient manipulation.

Title: Delete Graphic Image
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary graphic images. Location Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Delete Operation Select a graphic image with Edit Texture 2D tool, Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Delete The selected graphic image is now deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary graphic images using the Graphics Pop-up Menu and editing tools in a 2D environment.

Title: Create 2D Graphic Measurement
Content: Objective View graphic position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements. (ver2.5.0) Location Graphics Property Editor 2D Measurement Operation 2D Toolbar Select a graphic with Transform Graphic. Follow the indicated guideline below: Graphics Property Editor 2D Measurement Select the desired 2D measurement option. To Center View the 2D measurements from the center of the graphic to left/right/top/bottom of the Pattern outline. To Outline View the 2D measurements from the left/right/top/bottom of the graphic to the Pattern outline. The 2D measurements are now being displayed accordingly.
ContentDescription: "Access and manipulate 2D measurements of graphics within the Pattern outline using the Graphics Property Editor for precise positioning and visualization."

Title: Copy/Duplicate Graphic Image
Content: Objective Copy/paste or duplicate graphic images as needed. Location Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Copy (Ctrl + C), Paste (Ctrl + V) / Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Operation Copy/Paste Graphic Image Select a graphic image with Edit Texture tool or Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Copy (Ctrl + C), Paste (Ctrl + V) The copied graphic image is now being followed on the mouse. Place the copied graphic image at a desired location in the 2D window. Duplicate Graphic Image (ver2.3.0) Select a graphic image with Edit Texture tool or Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern The selected graphic image is now being duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. Note: Duplicate Graphic Image can only be used on Symmetrical Patterns.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a concise guide on how to copy, paste, and duplicate graphic images in the 2D window using the right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu and specific keyboard shortcuts.

Title: Apply Graphic Image
Content: Objective Place graphic images on Patterns. Use this function to express Garment details such as placed prints, embroideries, or logos. Location Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) 3D or 2D Toolbar Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D or 3D Toolbar Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) The file browser appears. Select a graphic image file and load. Click on a Pattern where the graphic image should be placed. The Add Graphic window appears. Enter the desired values for the graphic dimensions and position: Width Set the width of the graphic image. Height Set the height of the graphic image. Link or unlink the aspect ratio of the graphic image. Position Outline Set the distance from the left, right, top, or bottom of the graphic outline to the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). Center Set the distance from the center of the graphic to the left, right, top, or bottom of the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (Ver. 2.5.0). Click OK to place the graphic image. Note: Add graphics directly by right-clicking on a thumbnail of an image file in the Library window, then select Add as Graphic from the pop-up menu (ver2.4.0). When importing an AI file with multiple artboards as a graphic, the AI/PDF window appears where artboards can be reviewed and the desired artboard can be selected (Ver. 4.0.0). PBR maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated for the applied graphic image using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1)
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for placing graphic images on garment patterns, enabling users to effectively showcase details like prints, embroideries, and logos through intuitive 2D and 3D tools.

Title: PBR Map Generator (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective PBR Map can be automatically generated and applied to graphic images or imported BaseColor Map Texture Maps Location Property Editor Materials Operation Apply graphic with apply texture map or apply graphic Image. Click Create PBR Map button next to the map channels Create PBR map is supported for Displacement Map, Opacity Map, Roughness Map, and Metalness Map Note: The generated PBR Map is automatically stored in the AppData path. Click on the Map thumbnail image to check the save path. This feature applies to fabric, button, trim, graphic, buttonhole, topstitch, and puckering End Result You can automatically generate PBR maps for different channels.
ContentDescription: Create and apply customizable PBR maps for various texture channels in your graphic images with ease using our automated tools.

Title: Apply Substance SBSAR Materials to Trims, Buttons, and Avatars
Content: Objective Allows the user to apply high-quality Substance materials to assets other than cloth patterns within Marvelous Designer. Location Fabric Property Editor Material Substance Operation Load garment and avatar. Add trim or button to garment. Select the Fabric viewer in a window dropdown menu. In the Property Editor for a selected fabric, set the Material to 'Substance'. Click on the four-square button next to the Substance logo and import a Substance (.sbsar) file. Click on any Trim, Button, or part of the Avatar. Navigate to the Fabric window, select the Fabric the Substance material is assigned to, then select 'Assign' at the top of the Fabric window. Observe that the Substance material has been applied to the Trim, Button, or Avatar component.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to apply high-quality Substance materials to various assets in Marvelous Designer, enhancing their garment and avatar designs.

Title: Default Color Setting
Content: Objective Set the default color to change the native color of fabrics. Location Property Editor Material Color Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color The Color Palette window appears. Designate the desired color. Note: Eyedropper tool allows to extract any desired color not only from Marvelous Designer but any other websites or images. Select a color and add to save it in the bottom of the color palette.
ContentDescription: This web page guides users on how to set and customize the default fabric color in the Property Editor of Marvelous Designer, utilizing the Color Palette and eyedropper tool for enhanced design flexibility.

Title: Eyedropper
Content: Objective Use Eyedropper tool to extract any desired colors not only from Marvelous Designer, but any other websites or images just by clicking the colors. Location Property Editor Material Color Eyedropper Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color Eyedropper Move mouse cursor to desired area. The mouse cursor icon is now being changed to an eyedropper-shaped. Click on a desired area to extract a color. The extracted color sample appears in the window. To exit the tool, click on the Eyedropper icon again or press ESC on keyboard.
ContentDescription: "Learn how to effortlessly use the Eyedropper tool to extract colors from Marvelous Designer and any other website or image with just a click."

Title: Add Color Swatch
Content: Objective Add color swatches to custom palette. Location Property Editor Material Color Color Palette Window Add Operation Select a desired object Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. Click on Color in the Property Editor. The Color Palette window appears. Select a desired color from Open Palette or Palette Library. Follow the indicated guideline below: Color Palette Window Add The selected color is now being added to the custom palette.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for adding color swatches to a custom palette using the Color Palette window in the Property Editor.

Title: Color Palette
Content: Import existing color palettes from llustrator, Photoshop, or customize an own color palette and utilize it for design works (ver2.2.0).
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly import existing color palettes from Illustrator and Photoshop or create and customize your own for enhanced design projects with our user-friendly tool."

Title: Open/Save Color Palette File
Content: Objective Open a color palette file (*.ace / *.ase), or save colors as a palette file (*.aco). Location Property Editor Material Color Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color The Color Palette window appears. Click on Open Palette icon on the left side of the palette window. The Open File window appears. Select a desired palette file (*.ace / *.ase) and click Open to load. The selected palette file is now being loaded and applied. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color The Color Palette window appears. Click on Save as Palette icon on the left side of the palette window. The selected color is now being saved as *.aco file format.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for opening and saving color palette files in various formats, enhancing your material color management.

Title: Palette Library
Content: Objective Load or delete a palette file in the Library window. Location Property Editor Material Color Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color Color Palette window appears. Click on + button on the top-right of the window. Open File window appears. Select a desired palette file (*.aco/*.aso) to load. The selected file is now being added to the Palette Library. Note: Change Display Click on Display icon at the bottom-right corner of the Palette Library to change the display for the color swatches. Copy to Custom Palette Select a palette to be copied, then click on Copy to Custom Palette icon at the bottom-right corner of the window. Search Color (ver. 11) Search a similar color with the name of the color or the selected color.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for loading or deleting a color palette file in the Library window, along with options for displaying, copying, and searching for colors.

Title: Edit Color Swatch
Content: Objective Rename, reorder, and reset color swatches and color palettes. Location Property Editor Material Color Operation Rename Color Swatch Select a desired object Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color The color palette window appears. On the bottom-left side of the palette window, click on a color swatch to be renamed. 'Color Swatch Name' window appears. Rename as desired then either click on somewhere else or press Enter on the keyboard. The selected color swatch's name is now being adjusted. Note: Added Method in ver4.2.0 Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Materials Color The Color window appears. Under the Default_Palette, double click a color swatch to change its name. The Color Swatch Name window appears. Type in the desired name and click OK. Selected swatch's name is changed. Added Method in ver3.2.0 Select an item (Avatar, Fabric, Button, Topstitch, etc.) to change its color. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Color/ Specular Color/ Emission Color Click on the color swatch on the left. Type in the desired name when the name field is activated. Type in the desired name. The selected color swatch's name is changed. Reorder Color Swatch Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color Click and drag color swatches to reorder as desired. Reset Custom Palette Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color The Color Palette window appears. Click x on the Default_Palette button on the top of the Palette Library. All default colors are now being deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for renaming, reordering, and resetting color swatches and palettes within the Property Editor for various objects.

Title: [Beta] AI Texture Generator (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Easily type in keywords to generate different texture images to choose from to create new fabric textures. Location Fabric Style Window Fabric Property Material Basic Parameter AI Texture Generator button Operation Select a Fabric Style from Fabric Style window. Under Fabric Properties Materials Click AI Texture Generator button on the right side of the Basic Parameters. AI Texture Generator window appears. Set options, enter prompts, and click the Generate button. An AI texture image is created. Check the generated image in the preview window. The generated image is stored in History. Click generate again to generate more images. Click Apply button, the selected image is applied as the Fabric Texture. Generate AI Texture Options Fabric Type Select the fabric type. The pattern is generated on the texture of the selected fabric. Content Type Select content types. None Create an image without specifying characteristics of the texture image. Art Select the style of the texture image: Cartoon, Water Color Painting, Croquis, Oil Painting, Vintage Print Select the repeated-pattern type: Camouflage, Tartan Check, Paisley, Polka dot, Stripe Pattern Size Adjusts only the size of the pattern while maintaining the size of the material texture. Text Prompt Enter the prompts. Writing Tips: List the words. Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. Emphasize Certain Words. Parentheses are used in the word you want to emphasize, parentheses on certain words place more weight on those words. Weight increase rate: (word) 1.1times, ((word)) 1.21times. Maintain Prompt Even if the same prompts are used, the AI texture image is Newly generated each time. Thus, clicking the "Maintain Result" button may update the prompts while maintaining the characteristics of the previously generated result as much as possible. Note: It may differ from the existing result depending on the addition or change of the prompts. Random The sample prompt is randomly applied. The option automatically changes to a type specific to the prompt. History Previously generated images with prompts are recorded as "histories". The history remains accessible until Marvelous Designer is closed. If you select a previously created image in History and click Apply, the image is applied as Texture. Note : It may take a while to create when there are many users generating AI texture image at the same time. Fabric Type must be set and the Text Prompt must be input to generate. The resulting generated images are only a preview until Apply is selected.
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly create custom fabric textures by entering keywords and selecting options in our AI Texture Generator."

Title: Fabric List Window
Content: Default_Fabric is provided as default Fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until reopen a garment or rerun a program. You can reset edited properties of Default_Fabric with &gt Right Click &gt Pop Up Menu.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on how to manage and edit Default_Fabric settings, ensuring that changes persist until a garment is reopened or a program is rerun, with options for resetting properties.

Title: Create Additional Fabric
Content: Objective Create additional Fabric styles. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Add A new Fabric item is now being added to the Fabric list. Drag and drop a Fabric file (.ZFAB / .XTEX) onto the Fabric list in the Object Browser. The selected Fabric file is now being added to the list. Note: Drag and drop a Fabric file onto an existing style replaces its properties. Default_Fabric is provided as default fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until rerun of the program. It is able to reset edited properties of Default_Fabric at right-click pop-up menu but it is indelible.
ContentDescription: This web page serves as a guide for users to efficiently add and manage Fabric styles in the Object Browser, including instructions for dragging and dropping Fabric files and editing properties.

Title: Reset Fabric Property
Content: Objective Reset a Fabric in order to return to a default Fabric properties. Location 2D Pattern Window Edit Texture (2D) Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu Reset to Basic Fabric Object Browser Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Pattern Window Edit Texture(2D) Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu Reset to Basic Fabric Object Browser Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu Reset The selected Fabric's texture, color and physical properties are now being reset.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to reset a Fabric's texture, color, and physical properties to their default settings.

Title: Apply Fabric
Content: Objective Apply Fabrics (.zfab) to Patterns. Operation Apply from Property Editor Click on a Pattern, and choose a Fabric to apply from the Fabric menu in the Property Editor. The selected Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern accordingly. Note: Only Fabrics in the Fabric tab are being displayed in the corresponding Fabric menu. Assign to Selected Pattern Select a Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Assign to Selected Patterns The selected Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern accordingly. Assign to New Fabric Select a Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Assign to New Fabric Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu Assign to New Fabric The new Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric tab. Apply from Folder With Window File Search, open a folder where the Fabric files are being stored. Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a pattern in 2D or 3D window. The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric tab. Or, drag and drop Fabric files onto Fabric tab of the Object Browser. In case of drag-and-dropping onto Fabric item, the previous Fabric style gets replaced. In case of drag-and-dropping onto the empty space, the Fabric gets added in the list. Apply from Library Window Open a folder where the Fabric files are being stored from the Library window. Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a Pattern in 2D or 3D window. The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric List window. Drag and drop fabric files onto Fabric tab of the Object Browser: In case of drag-and-dropping onto Fabric item, the previous item gets replaced. In case of drag-and-dropping onto the empty space, the Fabric gets added in the list. Apply from Fabric Tab Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a Pattern in 2D or 3D window. The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply Fabrics to Patterns using various methods in the Property Editor and Object Browser.

Title: Rename Fabric
Content: Objective Rename Fabrics to distinguish one from another. Location Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Edit Name Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Click Name Field Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Fabric) Rename Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Edit Name Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Double Click Name Field Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Fabric) Rename The selected fabric's name is now being changed and applied.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for renaming fabrics in the Object Browser to easily distinguish between them.
